title: Fight, Flight, Freeze, Fawn: Understanding Trauma Responses
description: The four trauma responses explained. How each manifests, why we develop them, and how to work with your nervous system patterns.

content.text: You've heard of fight or flight. But trauma responses are more complex. Understanding yours can explain a lot about how you react to stress.
The nervous system perceives a threat and mobilizes to confront it.
The nervous system perceives a threat and mobilizes to escape.

items: Avoidance of conflict or difficult emotions

content.text: The nervous system perceives a threat it can't fight or escape and shuts down.
The nervous system learns safety comes from appeasing others.

items: Prioritizing others' needs over your own
Losing sense of self in relationships

content.text: Trauma responses develop as survival strategies. If fighting worked, you learned to fight. If freezing kept you safe (playing dead), you learned to freeze. If appeasing an abuser reduced harm, you learned to fawn.
Your trauma response protected you. It was adaptive in the original situation. The problem is when it activates inappropriately in safe situations.

items: What do I do when I feel threatened or stressed?
What was rewarded or punished in my childhood?
What response kept me safest growing up?
What do others say about how I handle conflict?
What does my body do when triggered?
Notice the urge to stay busy
Learn to tolerate discomfort without escaping
Notice when you abandon yourself for others
Learn your own preferences and needs

content.text: Your trauma response kept you alive. Now it may be keeping you stuck. Understanding your pattern is the first step to developing more flexibility. Trauma therapy can help you expand your window of tolerance and respond to situations with choice rather than automatic reaction.
